description: Cardiologist-level arrhythmia detection and classification in ambulatory electrocardiograms using a deep neural network

summary.one_liner: A Python research codebase for training and running a deep neural network that classifies arrhythmias in ambulatory (Holter-style) electrocardiogram recordings, from the Nature Medicine paper by Hannun et al.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides scripts to train a deep neural network on ECG data using a JSON config file (ecg/train.py) and to make predictions on a dataset with a saved model (ecg/predict.py). Models are saved as .hdf5 files after each epoch. A setup.sh script installs the requirements, with CPU-only or GPU builds selected by an environment variable. The README points to a cinc17 subdirectory README that walks through downloading the Physionet 2017 challenge dataset and training and evaluating a model on it. The README does not describe the network architecture or the detailed output format beyond this.
use_cases: train an arrhythmia classifier on ECG recordings
reproduce the Nature Medicine ECG paper results
run predictions on ECG data with a saved model
experiment with the Physionet 2017 challenge dataset
how_to_run: ./setup.sh   (CPU only; use env TF=gpu ./setup.sh for GPU)
stack: TensorFlow (implied by the TF=gpu setup option)
notable: Based on a peer-reviewed Nature Medicine paper, with a citation provided
Includes a worked example for the Physionet 2017 (CinC17) challenge dataset
Training is driven by JSON config files
Saves a model checkpoint after each epoch
caveats: Targets Python 2.7, an end-of-life Python version
README is brief; setup and dataset details are delegated to a separate cinc17 README
Released as research code, with no stated support or maintenance commitment
